topic: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
usual_baseline: Most fragility fracture patients leave without treatment started. Bone protection prescribed in 1.3–16% of hip fractures [1615][1693][1414]; 15.2% started after GP letters [1172]; 0% FRAX in falls [1146][1364]. Non-hip fractures fare worse: osteoporosis assessed in 25.7% vs 100% hip [1345]. GPs often do not act: 87% not started after discharge [1693].
fix_that_works: Giving a named team responsibility: 13.9% to 100% assessed, sustained [1615]. Community fracture liaison nurse: 47.9% to 84.0% treated [1516]. Ward-round prompts: FRAX 0% to 86% [1146], 50% to 88% [1362]. Kardex stickers: 50.9% to 84.6% [1470]. Stickers, whiteboards and pathways: zoledronic acid 12.12% to 95.45% [1173].
fix_that_fails: Teaching, protocols, MDTs and a new clinic: bisphosphonates stayed poor (64% not given) and FRAX fell 54% to 18% [1693]. Rewritten GP letter: 40% to 51% [1346]. EHR referral alert: 5% to 19% [1637]. Awareness: 5/38 to 23/43 referred [1444]. PTH not measured after intervention [1598].
consultant_advice: Heavily overdone in hip fracture, and relying on the GP letter fails. Audit non-hip fragility fractures, whether the first dose is given before discharge, or 12-month adherence (11.6% [1764]). Falls and exercise referral is also rarely measured [1177][1458].
